1.explanation: 1. audits/screenshot-thumbnails-test.js – Tests the audit that currently creates thumbnail `` elements and verifies how they’re rendered in the report. 2. gather/gatherers/full-page-screenshot-test.js – Contains the gatherer logic (and tests) for capturing the full-page screenshot (FPSs) which will be the new source for thumbnails. 3. computed/screenshots-test.js – Verifies the computed artifact that slices the full-page screenshot into smaller thumbnail images, critical for replacing the remote hotlinks. 4. lib/asset-saver-test.js – Tests how assets (like screenshots) are saved locally or embedded, a key piece in ensuring the FPSs-derived thumbnails are embedded rather than hotlinked. 5. computed/image-records-test.js – Covers the computed artifact that gathers image metadata (src, dimensions, etc.) for `` elements; useful to compare and transition from remote URLs to FPSs assets. 6. gather/gatherers/image-elements-test.js – Tests the gatherer that collects `` elements from the page, illustrating how image data has been surfaced in the report and why swapping to FPSs covers all thumbnails consistently.
1.bug_scenario: The Lighthouse report currently hotlinks thumbnail images by generating `` tags whose `src` attributes point back to the original remote URLs (e.g. “/img/community.jpg (apache.org)”). These thumbnails appear in the “Image elements do not have explicit width and height” audit (and similar CSP-sensitive locations), causing mixed-content/CSP issues and unexpected layout shifts. The goal is to replace these remote thumbnails with locally stored assets derived from the full-page screenshot (the FPSs), so that the report embeds a self-contained image instead of hotlinking to the server.
